prompt: Känner du Erik? Jag ser ___ varje dag.
hint: Do you know Erik? I see him every day.
explain: After the verb, use the object form: han → honom.

prompt: Maria är sjuk. Jag ringer ___ ikväll.
hint: Maria is ill. I’ll call her tonight.
explain: After the verb, use the object form: hon → henne.
After the verb, use the object form: jag → mig.

prompt: Mina kusiner bor i Åbo. Vi träffar ___ på lördag.
hint: My cousins live in Turku. We’re meeting them on Saturday.
explain: After the verb, use the object form: de → dem.
The one doing the action is the subject, so use de, not dem.

prompt: Vill du följa med ___ på bio?
hint: Do you want to come with us to the cinema?
explain: After a preposition like med, use the object form: vi → oss.

prompt: Hej Lisa och Tom! Jag träffar ___ imorgon.
hint: Hi Lisa and Tom! I’ll see you (both) tomorrow.
explain: You (plural) as an object is er; dig is only for one person.
After the verb, use the object form: du → dig.
Hus is an ett-word, so my is mitt: mitt hus.

prompt: ___ barn är fem och sju år.
hint: My children are five and seven.
explain: Children is plural, so my is mina: mina barn.
Väska is an en-word, so your is din: din väska.

hint: Our kitchen is small but cosy.
explain: Kök is an ett-word, so our is vårt: vårt kök.
Nycklar is plural, so your (plural) is era: era nycklar.

prompt: Lisa och Tom har en hund. ___ hund heter Bamse.
hint: Lisa and Tom have a dog. Their dog is called Bamse.
explain: Their is deras. Sin can never be part of the subject.
Anna is the subject and the parents are her own, so use sina (plural).
The parents belong to Sara, not to the subject Anna, so use hennes.
Peter is the subject and the car is his own, so use sin (bil is an en-word).
The car belongs to Peter, not to the subject Eva, so use hans.
De is the subject and the house is their own, so use sitt (hus is an ett-word).

prompt: Erik och ___ fru bor i Vasa.
hint: Erik and his wife live in Vaasa.
explain: Erik och hans fru is the whole subject, and sin can never be part of the subject.

hint: I call my mum every Sunday.
explain: Sin is only for third-person subjects; with jag, use min.
Känna sig is reflexive; with jag the pronoun is mig.

hint: She sits down on the sofa.
explain: Sätta sig is reflexive; with hon the pronoun is sig.

prompt: Maja och Leo ska gifta ___ i sommar.
hint: Maja and Leo are getting married this summer.
explain: Gifta sig is reflexive; with de (Maja och Leo) the pronoun is sig, not dem.

hint: We go to bed at ten.
explain: Lägga sig is reflexive; with vi the pronoun is oss.
Känna sig is reflexive; with du the pronoun is dig.
Speaking to several people (ni), the reflexive pronoun is er.

hint: You’re not allowed to smoke here. (people in general)
explain: Use man for rules and general statements about people.

prompt: I Finland går ___ ofta i bastu.
hint: In Finland people often go to the sauna.
explain: Man means people in general; the verb stays second after I Finland (the golden rule).

sentence: Hon ringer sina föräldrar varje dag.
accept: Varje dag ringer hon sina föräldrar.
en: She calls her (own) parents every day.
explain: Sina refers back to the subject hon; the verb stays second.
The reflexive pronoun mig comes right after the verb and the subject.
After the verb, use the object form: han → honom.
After the verb, use the object form: vi → oss.
Tom is the subject and the bike is his own, so use sin (cykel is an en-word).
The house belongs to Tom, not to the subject Sara, so use hans.

hint: The children are playing with their (own) toys.
explain: Barnen is the subject and the toys are their own, so use sina (plural).
Gifta sig is reflexive; with vi the pronoun is oss.
